Thanks for sharing those records. However, there’s a critical omission in your condition report: independent diagnostics have flagged transmission shudder and early CVT failure signs—a known, costly vulnerability on this generation Altima. A proper CVT rebuild or replacement at a reputable shop runs $3,500–$4,200. Because this is a confirmed material defect, I cannot evaluate the vehicle as “excellent condition.” 

For valuation context, a healthy 2016 Altima at 83,223 miles averages $11,765 on the private market. Per my purchasing standards, I must deduct the full estimated repair cost from that baseline, which brings the fair value down to approximately $7,800. I’m prepared to offer $7,800, which honestly accounts for the immediate transmission work required. 

If you have a complete diagnostic report or invoice proving the CVT was already addressed, please forward it. Otherwise, let me know if you can meet me at $7,800.
